with qstats as (
	SELECT TOP(@maxSampleCount)
		REPLACE(@@SERVERNAME,'\',':') AS [sql_instance],
		HOST_NAME() AS [computer_name],
		ISNULL(st1.objectid, 0) AS object_id,
		MAX(qs.plan_handle) AS query_plan_handle,
		MAX(qs.last_elapsed_time) AS last_elapsed_time,
        CONVERT(NVARCHAR, TODATETIMEOFFSET(MAX(qs.last_execution_time), DATEPART(TZOFFSET, SYSDATETIMEOFFSET())), 126) AS last_execution_time,
        CONVERT(NVARCHAR, TODATETIMEOFFSET(MAX(qs.creation_time), DATEPART(TZOFFSET, SYSDATETIMEOFFSET())), 126) AS plan_creation_time,
		qs.query_hash AS query_hash,
		qs.query_plan_hash AS query_plan_hash,
		SUM(qs.execution_count) AS execution_count,
		SUM(qs.total_elapsed_time) AS total_elapsed_time,
		SUM(qs.total_worker_time) AS total_worker_time,
		SUM(qs.total_logical_reads) AS total_logical_reads,
		SUM(qs.total_physical_reads) AS total_physical_reads,
		SUM(qs.total_logical_writes) AS total_logical_writes,
		SUM(qs.total_rows) AS total_rows,
		SUM(qs.total_grant_kb) as total_grant_kb
	FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats AS qs
	    LEFT JOIN sys.dm_exec_cached_plans AS cp ON cp.plan_handle = qs.plan_handle
	    -- The plan attributes give the database and object id of a plan without reading the batch text, which
	    -- dm_exec_sql_text would materialize for every cached statement before the lookback filter applies.
	    -- objectid is the object id only for plans of objects; for ad hoc and prepared plans it is a hash of the
	    -- text, and dm_exec_sql_text returns NULL there.
	    CROSS APPLY (
	        SELECT
	            MAX(CASE WHEN a.attribute = 'objectid' THEN CONVERT(int, a.value) END) AS objectid,
	            MAX(CASE WHEN a.attribute = 'dbid' THEN CONVERT(int, a.value) END) AS dbid
	        FROM sys.dm_exec_plan_attributes(qs.plan_handle) AS a
	        WHERE a.attribute IN ('objectid', 'dbid')
	    ) AS pa
	    CROSS APPLY (
	        SELECT
	            CASE WHEN cp.objtype IS NULL OR cp.objtype IN ('Adhoc', 'Prepared') THEN NULL ELSE pa.objectid END AS objectid,
	            pa.dbid AS dbid
	    ) AS st1
	GROUP BY
	    st1.objectid,
		qs.query_hash,
		qs.query_plan_hash
	HAVING MAX(DATEADD(ms, qs.last_elapsed_time / 1000, qs.last_execution_time)) > DATEADD(SECOND, @lookbackTime, GETDATE())
),
proc_stats AS (
	SELECT
		ps.object_id,
		ps.database_id,
		SUM(ps.execution_count) AS procedure_execution_count
	FROM sys.dm_exec_procedure_stats AS ps
	GROUP BY ps.object_id, ps.database_id
)
SELECT qs.*,
	SUBSTRING(st.text, (stats.statement_start_offset / 2) + 1,
			 ((CASE statement_end_offset
				   WHEN -1 THEN DATALENGTH(st.text)
				   ELSE stats.statement_end_offset END - stats.statement_start_offset) / 2) + 1) AS query_text,
	ISNULL(DB_NAME(st.dbid), '') AS database_name,
	-- A statement after offset 0 returns its own text, the head of the batch where the comment tags are, and the
	-- characters right before it. Its offsets are relative to that text. A statement at offset 0 keeps the whole batch text, because its
	-- normalized hash covers the whole batch.
	CASE
		WHEN @collectFullText = 0 THEN N''
		WHEN stats.statement_start_offset > 0
			THEN SUBSTRING(st.text, (stats.statement_start_offset / 2) + 1,
				((CASE stats.statement_end_offset WHEN -1 THEN DATALENGTH(st.text) ELSE stats.statement_end_offset END - stats.statement_start_offset) / 2) + 1)
		ELSE st.text
	END AS full_query_text,
	CASE WHEN @collectFullText = 1 AND stats.statement_start_offset > 0 THEN ISNULL(SUBSTRING(st.text, 1, @headChars), N'') ELSE N'' END AS full_query_text_head,
	-- The characters right before the statement. They show whether a block comment directly precedes it. A start
	-- before position 1 returns only the characters up to the statement.
	CASE WHEN @collectFullText = 1 AND stats.statement_start_offset > 0 THEN ISNULL(SUBSTRING(st.text, (stats.statement_start_offset / 2) - @prefixChars + 1, @prefixChars), N'') ELSE N'' END AS full_query_text_prefix,
	0 AS statement_start_offset,
	(CASE stats.statement_end_offset WHEN -1 THEN DATALENGTH(st.text) ELSE stats.statement_end_offset END) - stats.statement_start_offset AS statement_end_offset,
	ISNULL(qp.query_plan, '') AS query_plan,
	ISNULL(CASE WHEN qs.object_id > 0 THEN qs.object_id END, '') AS procedure_id,
         ISNULL(CASE WHEN qs.object_id > 0
                         THEN QUOTENAME(OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(qs.object_id, st.dbid))
                                         + N'.' + QUOTENAME(OBJECT_NAME(qs.object_id, st.dbid))
                    END, '') AS procedure_name,
	ISNULL(pst.procedure_execution_count, 0) AS procedure_execution_count
FROM qstats AS qs
		INNER JOIN sys.dm_exec_query_stats AS stats
			ON qs.query_plan_handle = stats.plan_handle
			AND qs.query_hash = stats.query_hash
			AND qs.query_plan_hash = stats.query_plan_hash
		-- The plan of this statement only. dm_exec_query_plan returns the plan of the whole batch,
		-- which repeats once per statement row when a batch holds many statements.
		OUTER APPLY sys.dm_exec_text_query_plan(qs.query_plan_handle, stats.statement_start_offset, stats.statement_end_offset) AS qp
		CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(qs.query_plan_handle) AS st
		LEFT JOIN proc_stats AS pst
			ON qs.object_id = pst.object_id
			AND st.dbid = pst.database_id
		WHERE st.text IS NOT NULL;
